amendments.rule: Carry a case preposition: `τοῦ πληρώματος` → *of the fulness*. Then *of* and *the* form one unit headed on *the*, and the noun stands alone. The English *the* is what anchors that unit, so where the ASV gives the noun no determiner the article carries nothing: it is `unrepresented` under rule 23 and the case preposition stays with the noun. `τῇ προσευχῇ` → *by prayer*, `τῆς εἰρήνης` → *of peace*, `τῷ θεῷ` → *to God*, `τοῖς ἀνθρώποις` → *unto men* are all one unit on the noun. Do not read this rule as licensing a bare *of* or *by* on the article; a determinerless English phrase is rule 23's case, not this one. This rule speaks throughout of a preposition realizing the governed word's **own case**, and an English preposition licensed by something else does not move to that word merely because it stands in front of it. Where the ASV builds a support-verb frame around the Greek verb and the frame's own supplied noun is what licenses the preposition, the preposition belongs to the frame and stays inside the verb's unit, the governed word keeping a bare noun: `οὐ λογίζεται τὸ κακόν` → *taketh not account of evil* gives *taketh … account of* to `λογίζεται` headed on *account* and a bare *evil* to `κακόν`, the article standing `unrepresented` under rule 23 as it would in any event, and `ἀναμνήσει … τὰς ὁδούς μου` → *shall put you in remembrance of my ways* gives *shall put … in remembrance of* to `ἀναμνήσει` headed on *remembrance* and a bare *ways* to `ὁδούς`. Rule 27 is what forces that, the supplied *account* or *remembrance* being what licenses the *of*, and rule 106's accusative arm says the same from the other side: an accusative has no case for an English preposition to realize, so a preposition standing over an accusative object is the verb's or the frame's and never the object's. That reaches the occurrence the frame **licenses** and no further. Where the ASV **repeats** that same preposition over a second complement of the frame, the repetition is decided by rule 103 and not here: it is a rule 7 helper on the member it introduces, whatever that member's case, and it is neither `added` nor stretched back over the frame under rule 15. `Οὕτως ἡμᾶς λογιζέσθω ἄνθρωπος ὡς ὑπηρέτας Χριστοῦ` → *Let a man so account of us as of ministers of Christ* gives *Let … account of* to `λογιζέσθω`, a bare *us* to the accusative `ἡμᾶς`, and the second *of* to `ὑπηρέτας` though that word is accusative too, rule 103 already forbidding both the stretch and the `added` for a repeated word from rule 7's own list and scoping rule 106's accusative arm the same way. That rule's own clause speaks of a Greek preposition or conjunction governing two coordinate members, and a supplied frame noun licensing two complements is the same case: what makes a repetition a helper is that the word it repeats has already been spent, not what licensed it. So ask which occurrence is in question before asking what case the word in front of it carries. A genitive or a dative is the contrast and is this rule's ordinary case, its own case being what the English preposition answers to, which is why `τῶν ἀνθρώπων` → *of men* and `τῇ ἀληθείᾳ` → *with the truth* are decided here and not there.
amendments.why: 1CO.4 met a case rule 21 had not considered. The rule's frame doctrine and rule 106's accusative arm both say a preposition over an accusative object is 'never the object's', without qualification. 1CO.4.17 obeyed that (patched here) but 1CO.4.1 could not: the ASV writes *account of us as of ministers*, and the second *of* is a repetition, which rule 103 in terms makes a helper on the member it introduces and forbids stretching back under rule 15 or marking `added`, *of* being a word from rule 7's own list. Left as it stood, the categorical sentence would force a later pass either to stretch a repeated *of* discontinuously — which rule 103 forbids — or to strand it. The amendment scopes the accusative arm to the licensing occurrence and routes the repetition to rule 103, adding 1CO.4.17 as the second worked example of the frame doctrine alongside the existing `λογίζεται` one. It narrows rather than widens: nothing that was decided by the old text is decided differently, since no repetition case was reachable under it.

conventions: A support frame's preposition and its repetition are placed differently in this chapter, and the difference is principled. The occurrence the frame licenses stays inside the verb's unit and the governed word stands bare where that word is accusative: 4:1 gives *Let ... account of* to λογιζέσθω with a bare *us*, and 4:17 gives *shall put ... in remembrance of* to ἀναμνήσει with a bare *ways* (rules 21 and 106). Where the ASV repeats that preposition over a second complement of the same frame, the repetition goes to the member it introduces and is neither stretched back nor marked `added`: 4:1 gives the second *of* to ὑπηρέτας though it too is accusative (rule 103). A dative governed word is the contrast and takes the preposition itself, as 4:8 συμβασιλεύσωμεν ὑμῖν -> *with you* does.

A supplied intensifying *even* standing in front of a temporal preposition or conjunction is folded onto that token as a rule 7 helper and is not marked `added`: ἄχρι -> *Even unto* at 4:11 and ἕως -> *even until* at 4:13, each headed on the word rendering the source token. No appositive follows either, so rule 105's supplied appositional *even* is not in question, and no other source token stands to license the word.

φυσιόω is not a prefixed compound. The *up* of *puffed up* answers to no element of the Greek word; it is an English phrasal particle and a rule 7 helper riding inside the verb's own unit, as 4:6, 4:18 and 4:19 all have it. Do not cite rule 106's preverb arm for this lexeme, and do not read the corpus rows for it as evidence that a preverb is realized.

report: Cross-verse: one real split, in the support-verb frame's own preposition standing over an accusative object. 1CO.4.1 keeps *Let ... account of* whole on λογιζέσθω and leaves the accusative ἡμᾶς a bare *us*, exactly as rule 21's οὐ λογίζεται τὸ κακόν -> *taketh not account of evil* requires. 1CO.4.17 built the same kind of frame — *shall put you in remembrance of* — and handed the frame's *of* to the accusative τὰς ὁδούς, while leaving the other accusative of that same double-accusative clause, ὑμᾶς, bare on the stated ground that an accusative has no case for an English preposition to realize. One test, twice in one verse, opposite results. Patched 4.17: *of* moves inside ἀναμνήσει's unit, still headed on *remembrance*, and ὁδούς takes a bare *ways*.

4.1's second *of* (*as of ministers*) is a different question and was left alone: it is a repetition of the frame preposition over a second complement, and rule 103's repeated-function-word clause puts such a word on the member it introduces and forbids both `added` and stretching it back under rule 15. But rules 21 and 106 say 'never the object's' without qualification, so 4.1's correct reading sits in apparent violation of a categorical sentence — that gap is the amendment to rule 21. 4.8 is the control from the other side and was already right: συμβασιλεύσωμεν ὑμῖν gives *with* to the dative under rule 106's dative arm.

BSB: none of the three disagreements is an error. 4.7 καί — the ASV writes no word for the intensifying particle in *but if thou didst receive it*, and rule 65 decides it on the English alone. 4.9 ὁ before θεός — no *the* is written, rule 23, and the chapter treats every such article alike (4.5, 4.9, 4.20). 4.12 ταῖς — displaced by ἰδίαις taking *our own*, which is rule 47's construction named in terms. All three are the documented convention difference on function morphemes; no accepted edge was changed to move the figure.

Note-only defect corrected in 4.18 and 4.19: φυσιόω carries no preverb, so rule 106 was mis-cited for the *up* of *puffed up*. The edges were already right and are unchanged in both patches — *up* is an English phrasal particle answering to no source element and riding inside the verb's unit under rule 7, which is what 4.6 already did without the false citation.

Checked and cleared as source-licensed, not splits: μή with an indefinite joined at 4.5 (*nothing*, one English word) and split at 4.6 (*no* / *one*, two), which is the count test of rules 59 and 94; διά headed on the prepositional word at 4.6, 4.10 and 4.17 alike under rules 45 and 78; anarthrous nouns taking a supplied determiner (4.1, 4.4, 4.5, 4.13, 4.17, 4.21) against articular ones where the article takes it (4.5, 4.6, 4.15, 4.19); supplied copulas placed on the predicate throughout (4.10, 4.17, 4.20) and never on a subject pronoun; ὡς as *as if* / *as though* / *as*, the ASV's own words. The table is blind to `added` units, so I read the dump end to end for that: the chapter marks nothing `added` anywhere, and every supplied English word — *to go* (4.6), *have ye* (4.15), *Even* (4.11), *even* (4.13), the resumptive *it* and *you* (4.7, 4.14) — is folded onto a licensing token, consistently.
